Regio- and stereoselective azidation of activated
N-allenamides: an entry to α, β, γ and δ-amido-
azides†
Dorian Schutz, ‡ Maxime Hourtoule ‡ and Laurence Miesch *
rsc.li/frontiers-organic
A totally controlled regiodivergent azidation of activated N-allenamides is presented. Using TMSN /TBAF,
β-azidation of N-allenamides occurs exclusively, yielding vinyl azides. Conversely, employing a TFA/
TMSN mixture results solely in the formation of γ-azides. A subsequent [1,3] azide shift of the latter with
DBU produces α-amido vinyl azides. Additionally, δ-difluorinated azides featuring an ynamide are selec-
tively synthesized from ene-ynamides. The practical applicability of these transformations is demonstrated
through the formation of cyanide derivatives, trifluoromethyl ketones and primary enamines.
Introduction
Organic azides are versatile synthetic intermediates.<sup>1</sup> As
efective ammonia surrogates,<sup>2</sup> they serve as keystones for the
synthesis of N-heterocycles,<sup>3</sup> and ofer access to essential bio-
active molecules.<sup>4</sup> Among them, the unique features of vinyl-
azides have turned these compounds into critical building
blocks for the construction of N-heterocycles.<sup>5</sup> The remarkable
properties of the azide group connected to an alkene moiety<sup>6</sup>
allows this functional group to act as an electrophile,<sup>7</sup> an
enamine-type nucleophile<sup>8</sup> or a radical acceptor.<sup>9</sup> The multi-
faced reactivity of this highly versatile synthons have generated
a great inspiring variety of intermediates such as iminodiazo-
nium ions, nitrilium ions,<sup>10</sup> iminyl radicals<sup>11</sup> and metal enam-
inyl radicals<sup>12</sup> upon heating-, metal-or light-induced proces-
ses.<sup>5d</sup> Classical procedures to prepare vinyl azides involve base-
promoted elimination of haloazidoalkanes<sup>13</sup> and hydroazida-
tion of alkynes.<sup>14</sup> The incorporation of a trifluoromethyl group
into biologically active compounds frequently enhances their
physicochemical properties, including lipophilicity and meta-
bolic stability.<sup>15</sup> Consequently, molecules that contain both a
fluorine group and an azide moiety serve as highly efective

our interest in the preparation of nitrogen-containing building

Conclusion
A totally regio- and stereoselective azidation of activated
N-allenamides has been developed. Azidation of central sp
carbon takes place with CF and ester substituted
N-allenamides. Difluorinated N-allenamides produced an E/Z
mixture of vinyl azides bearing a monofluorinated alkene with
good overall yields. γ-Azidation was tolerated for terminal as

A totally regio- and stereoselective azidation of activated
N-allenamides has been developed. Azidation of central sp
carbon takes place with CF and ester substituted
N-allenamides. Difluorinated N-allenamides produced an E/Z
mixture of vinyl azides bearing a monofluorinated alkene with
good overall yields. γ-Azidation was tolerated for terminal as
well as CF -substituted N-allenamides. A [1,3] azide shift with
DBU provided α-substituted amido-vinyl azides starting from
fluorinated N-allenamides. Hydroazidation via an ene-ynamide
